pairs.subject: translation-quality-measurement
pairs.evidence: scripts/i18n/catalog-check.mjs:303 The catalog gate only ever compares a target with the source at the same address. It never groups units by identical source value, so duplicate-source divergence, one of the four decidable classes, goes unchecked: a read-only count over messages/ found 357 (cs), 312 (de) and 335 (fr) of 1,081 identical-English groups whose targets differ. Termbase adherence is also not scripted here; contract.md §9 describes it only as a manual detector.

techniques.evidence: scripts/i18n/catalog-check.mjs:303 Skeleton parity is realized well: the ICU AST is compared in both directions separately (lines 320-331), alongside carried literals, control characters and ICU compile. But the decidable duplicate-source-divergence class has no rule at all, and there is no termbase check in the gate.

scripts/i18n/catalog-check.mjs:360 sourceSuspects attributes a failure seen in two or more locales to the shared source, cites each locale and check, and is advisory only (i18n-check.mjs:539 'fix the source string first (advisory)'). The signal is cross-locale check agreement rather than two-model disagreement, but the finding goes to the source owner as the technique requires.

pairs.evidence: pipeline/jobfit/tests/test_i18n.py:53 The language tests here cover lang normalisation, the write-in-language directive, Czech taxonomy aliases and narrative-language honesty, not the quality of a translated store. A search of pipeline/jobfit/tests for glossary, termbase, chrF and pretranslat found nothing.
